recent_articles.title: Despite looming inflationary pressures, why RBI could defer rate hikes at policy meeting this week | Explained News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is expected to maintain its current policy stance, remaining in a wait-and-watch mode on June 5th. The MPC will assess the impact of rising crude oil prices and global economic uncertainties, including geopolitical tensions, on inflation and growth projections.  Despite mounting inflationary pressures, the RBI is likely to defer any interest rate hikes until later this year due to benign retail inflation and a cautious approach towards potential risks. The central bank will closely monitor evolving developments in the global environment and adjust its policy response accordingly.

recent_articles.title: Ghaziabad murder news, Key Accused Asad In Ghaziabad Teen Surya Pratap Chauhan Murder on bakrid Killed In Encounter With Cops
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Asad**, the main accused in the stabbing of 17-year-old Surya Pratap Chauhan, was shot dead during a police encounter on Saturday.  He had been carrying a Rs 50,000 reward for his arrest and sustained gunshot injuries during retaliatory firing after he opened fire on police officers. **Surya Pratap Chauhan** was stabbed in the Khoda area of Ghaziabad on May 28th, the day of Bakrid, triggering outrage and protests.  Police have arrested three of the five individuals named as accused in the case. The incident has prompted calls for similar action against other suspects involved.

recent_articles.title: Punjab civic polls results: AAP sweeps elections, BJP and Congress win key corporations - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)** swept the Punjab civic body polls, winning 958 of 1,977 municipal wards. The BJP and Congress secured key municipal corporations in Abohar and Kapurthala respectively.  **Bhagwant Mann**, the Punjab Chief Minister, hailed the results as a reflection of public support for his government. However, political analysts cautioned against directly linking the civic poll outcome to the 2027 Assembly polls. Opposition parties accused the AAP government of using official machinery to influence the election.

recent_articles.title: Aam Aadmi Party scores big in Punjab civic elections - The Tribune
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)** secured a resounding victory in Punjab's urban local body elections, winning control of five municipal corporations and nine nagar panchayats.  **Bhagwant Mann**, the Chief Minister, hailed the outcome as "historic" and attributed it to AAP's model of good governance. The party also performed strongly in 19 nagar panchayats, securing a majority in most areas. **Manish Sisodia**, AAP Punjab affairs in-charge, emphasized the landslide victory as a testament to the people's endorsement of their model.  The Congress finished second, while Independents secured third place.

recent_articles.title: Implementation of 'guarantees', decline of BRS favour Congress in Telangana, BJP aiming for better show - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Lok Sabha elections are expected to be a tight race between the **Congress** and the **BJP**, with both parties aiming for victory. The **Congress**, riding high on its recent Assembly election win, is banking on the implementation of its campaign promises and the popularity of CM Revanth Reddy to secure votes. The **BJP**, which saw its vote share double in the 2023 Assembly elections, aims to capitalize on this momentum and secure a significant portion of seats.  The **BRS**, facing a morale slump after its defeat, is expected to struggle against these two major contenders.

recent_articles.title: True Gen-Z defined by both its culture and contribution towards nation building: BJP president Nitin Nabin | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** national president Nitin Nabin addressed concerns about India's Gen Z, calling for an open debate on its definition and contribution to nation building.  He emphasized the need to guide this energy in a positive direction, citing examples of youth-led movements in neighboring countries that have led to instability. Nabin also cautioned against labeling young people as "anti-establishment" and highlighted the importance of nurturing their potential for progress. He stressed the role of the government in providing direction and support for India's youth, particularly in areas like employment and education.

recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** national president Nitin Nabin called for an open debate on defining India's Gen Z, its politics, and its positive direction.  He emphasized that true Gen Z is defined by both culture and contribution to nation-building, urging the youth to avoid being swayed by negative influences or labeled as anti-establishment. recent_articles.title: NA panel takes govt to task over budget preparation, reforms - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A parliamentary committee in Pakistan expressed concern over the government's failure to circulate and publish the Budget Strategy Paper by May 10th, as well as its continued reliance on indirect taxes and petroleum levy. **Syed Naveed Qamar**, former finance minister of the PPP, criticized the lack of progress on structural reforms and highlighted the growing burden of circular debt in the energy sector.  **Dr Ali Salman**, a private economist representing the UNDP, warned that inflation could undermine economic growth due to rising prices for essential goods. The committee also expressed concern about Pakistan's dependence on foreign imports and the vulnerability of the economy to regional geopolitical instability.

recent_articles.title: Mayawati demands extensive relief for storm victims in Uttar Pradesh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mayawati**, president of the Bahujan Samaj Party, called on the **Uttar Pradesh** government to provide extensive support to families affected by recent storms and heavy rain that have caused at least 111 deaths. recent_articles.title: Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav over Samajwadi Party spokesperson's 'anti-Brahmin remark' - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mayawati**, chief of the **Bahujan Samaj Party**, criticized **Akhilesh Yadav**, leader of the **Samajwadi Party**, for remaining silent on alleged derogatory remarks made by an SP spokesperson, Rajkumar Bhati, against Brahmins.  She argued that the silence is escalating the situation and urged **Yadav** to take action and apologize. The police in Ghaziabad have booked Bhati under Section 196(1) of the Indian Penal Code for promoting enmity between groups on grounds of religion.

recent_articles.title: Silence, the court is in session - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Yashwant Varma**, a judge of the Allahabad High Court, resigned after an inquiry found he and his family had exercised control over cash recovered from his official residence in 2025.  The Supreme Court Collegium recommended impeachment proceedings against him, but before they could proceed, Varma stepped down. The article also examines the growing concerns about judicial corruption, citing data from the Lok Sabha that shows a sharp rise in complaints against judges between 2016 and 2025. It highlights the lack of transparency surrounding these complaints, with the Law Ministry often stating it does not maintain records or has no mechanism to monitor them.  The article also discusses Rishi A. Kumar's blog post criticizing the judiciary for suppressing discussion about its failures, which led to a backlash from legal professionals and ultimately prompted him to seek legal intervention.

recent_articles.title: Bulgaria elections: Who’s running and what’s at stake? | Elections News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Bulgaria will hold a snap parliamentary election on April 19th, following political instability and widespread corruption protests. **Rumen Radev**, former president of the Progressive Bulgaria party, is running for prime minister, along with former Prime Minister **Boyko Borissov** from the GERB-UDF party.  The election comes amidst deep divisions and a desire for stability after seven national elections in the past four years. The outcome could significantly impact Bulgaria's foreign policy, particularly its relationship with the European Union and Russia. While Radev has pledged to combat corruption and restore order, his pro-Russian stance may complicate relations with Brussels.  The election is expected to draw over 3.3 million voters, who are concerned about economic challenges and political instability.

recent_articles.title: Kanshi Ram returns - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi** and the **Congress party** are marking the birth anniversary of Kanshi Ram, a Dalit icon who founded the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), to gain support from Dalit voters.  The BSP's legacy is being invoked by various political parties across India, including the **Samajwadi Party**, which has adopted the slogan "PDA Diwas" in honor of Kanshi Ram. The BSP, under Mayawati's leadership, formed governments with the BJP in Uttar Pradesh and continues to be a significant force in Dalit politics.  The legacy of Kanshi Ram is being re-examined by political parties seeking to appeal to marginalized communities.

recent_articles.title: Rift widens among Bihar Opposition after Rajya Sabha poll defeat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the recent Rajya Sabha elections in Bihar, where the ruling NDA secured all five seats, a rift has emerged within the Opposition Mahagathbandhan coalition. **Tejashwi Yadav**, leader of the RJD, faces criticism from both **Congress** and the **Communist Party of India-Marxist-Leninist (Liberation)** for absenteeism by three Congress MLAs and one RJD MLA. recent_articles.title: Hours before Rajya Sabha polling, AIMIM announces to vote for RJD candidate - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
**NDA** is facing a tight race in the Rajya Sabha elections, falling short of the 3 votes needed to win all five seats. The main opposition party, **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)**, relies on support from five **All India Majlis-E-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM)** MLAs and a lone **Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP)** MLA to secure victory.  **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** has two candidates: **Nitin Nabin** and **Shivesh Kumar**, while **Janata Dal (United) (JD-U)** fields **Chief Minister Nitish Kumar** and sitting Rajya Sabha member **Ramnath Thakur**. The remaining candidate is from the **Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM)**, led by **Upendra Kushwaha**.  The RJD has 25 MLAs, including support from Congress, left parties, and the Indian Inclusive Party (IIP).

**NDA** needs 205 MLAs to win all five seats. The opposition camp requires 6 more votes for a victory. This makes cross-voting a possibility as no party whip can be issued for Rajya Sabha polling.  To secure their desired outcome, **RJD**, led by **Tejashwi Yadav**, has shifted its MLA to a private hotel in Patna.  **Lesi Singh**, a JD-U minister, criticized the move, calling it "house arrest" for the MLAs. 

The NDA camp is confident of securing more votes than anticipated and all five candidates will win their seats. **Sanjay Jha**, the JD-U national working president, expressed confidence in the NDA's success. Meanwhile, **I P Gupta**, an IIP MLA, claimed that JD(U) MLAs are upset with the BJP for removing Nitish Kumar from his position as CM and would vote based on their conscience.

recent_articles.title: As Rahul Gandhi eyes Dalit consolidation through Kanshi Ram in U.P., BSP gets unsettled, political slugfest intensified - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
**Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Lok Sabha**'s Opposition, is aiming to mobilize Dalits in Uttar Pradesh for the **Congress party**. He seeks to strengthen the party’s social justice narrative by demanding the **Bharat Ratna** for **Kanshi Ram**, founder of the **Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP)**. This move has unsettled the BSP and its leader **Mayawati**, while the **Congress party in U.P.** is enthusiastic about Gandhi's efforts, hoping to consolidate Dalit support in favor of the Congress ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

Gandhi’s outreach towards Dalits has been evident in recent days.  He addressed a ‘Samvidhan Sammelan’ program on March 13th organized by the state **Congress** in Lucknow, marking Kanshi Ram’s birth anniversary. He claimed that if his great-grandfather, India's first Prime Minister **Jawaharlal Nehru**, were alive at the time of Kanshi Ram's rise, he would have been made Chief Minister from the **Congress**.  He acknowledged past shortcomings by the **Congress** in fulfilling its responsibilities, which led to leaders like **Kanshi Ram** charting their own political path. 

On Kanshi Ram’s birth anniversary on Sunday (March 15, 2026), Gandhi wrote to **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** demanding the highest civilian honor for him. The outreach is a renewed effort to engage with Dalits, a large social group comprising roughly 21% of the total electorate in U.P., positioning the **Congress** as staunch advocates for issues faced by marginalized communities.  The **BSP**, founded by **Kanshi Ram**, has accused the **Congress** of constantly trying to weaken it through various tactics. The **Samajwadi Party (SP)**, while not directly reacting to Gandhi's attempts, signals that all demands are already raised by the U.P.-centric party. Analysts point out that bold assertions by **Gandhi** need to translate into action on the ground to shift a sizeable Dalit support in favor of the **Congress**.

recent_articles.title: Rahul writes to PM Modi, seeks Bharat Ratna for BSP founder Kanshi Ram - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article:
## Congress Leader Calls for Bharat Ratna for Kanshi Ram

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to posthumously award the Bharat Ratna to Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) founder Kanshi Ram. In a letter, Gandhi highlighted Kanshi Ram's impact on Indian politics and his dedication to empowering marginalized communities. He argues that Kanshi Ram transformed political awareness among Dalits and the poor, making them feel their voices mattered. Gandhi emphasizes that Kanshi Ram's legacy of social justice and constitutional rights is worthy of national recognition.  He cites widespread support for this honor from Dalit intellectuals and activists.
